questions.stem: Inflation caused mainly by a rise in total demand that exceeds supply is called:
questions.explanation: Demand-pull — aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply at current prices. Cost-push — higher input costs (oil, wages) drive prices up. Imported — costlier imports or a weaker currency. Structural — bottlenecks in specific sectors such as food or housing.

questions.stem: The situation of simultaneous high inflation and high unemployment is called:
questions.explanation: Stagflation — stagnant output with rising prices — breaks the classic Phillips curve relation. Best-known example: OECD economies in the 1970s after the oil shocks. Reflation = deliberate policy to push prices up after a deflationary spell; deflation = falling prices; recession = two quarters of negative GDP growth.

questions.stem: Which group carries the largest weight in the CPI (Combined) basket in India?
questions.explanation: Food and beverages accounts for roughly 46 % of the CPI (Combined) basket — which is why food-price shocks dominate headline retail inflation in India. Housing weight applies only to the urban CPI. The rest of the basket is pan/tobacco, clothing, fuel and light, household goods, health, education, transport and miscellaneous.

questions.stem: Hyperinflation, in standard economic literature, is inflation typically exceeding:
questions.explanation: The classic Cagan threshold for hyperinflation is 50 % per month. Famous cases: Weimar Germany (1923), Hungary (1946, worst ever), Zimbabwe (2008), Venezuela (2016-19). Rough categorisation: creeping < 3 % p.a., walking 3-10 %, galloping 10-100 %, anything faster and accelerating = hyperinflation.

questions.stem: If the RBI wants to reduce inflation through monetary policy, it will typically:

options.option_text: Buy government bonds in the open market

questions.explanation: A higher repo rate raises banks' cost of funds, lifts lending rates, cools borrowing and demand, and eases inflation. Rate cuts, CRR cuts and open-market bond purchases are expansionary and add to inflationary pressure. The repo rate is decided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), a six-member body that meets at least every two months.

questions.stem: Under India's inflation-targeting framework, the RBI has to keep CPI inflation (on average) at:
questions.explanation: Since the 2016 amendment to the RBI Act, India runs a flexible inflation-targeting regime — CPI inflation target is 4 % with a tolerance band of ±2 %, i.e., between 2 % and 6 %. The target is reviewed by the Government in consultation with the RBI every five years; the 4 % target was retained for the 2021-26 period.

questions.stem: A fall in the overall price level over a sustained period is called:
questions.explanation: Deflation — sustained fall in the general price level. Disinflation is when inflation itself slows (prices still rising, just more slowly). Reflation is the policy effort to push prices back up after a deflationary period. Stagflation is high inflation combined with stagnant growth. Japan's 'lost decades' (1990s-2000s) are the textbook modern deflation example.
